answer: Messages cross the mountains by flag relay, and each station logs the time it receives and passes the signal, so a message can be traced from valley to valley. A garden message invented at the last station fails the log: at the wander of the relay the times must line up station by station, and an invented message arrives before it was sent. Faking the relay means posting signalmen on 12 peaks for a season and paying 19,600, while the summit entry in each station's log is read by the telegraph master, so a message whose relay was never logged is discarded.
